# Scripts

- ESM `.mjs`, Node 24 built-ins plus `@playwright/test`; no new dependencies. Prettier style: 2 spaces, single quotes, semicolons, trailing commas. JSDoc on exported functions.
- Vendored, byte-identical copies of the extension repo: `scripts/agents/**` and `scripts/worktree/**`. Never edit them here; change them upstream, then re-vendor (`.agents/README.md`). `node scripts/worktree/wt.mjs doctor` reports drift.
- Ports: never write `4180`/`4181`. Use `port('SITE_PORT', { cwd })` / `port('SITE_CAPTURE_PORT', { cwd })` from `scripts/worktree/ports.mjs` with `cwd` = repo root from `import.meta.url`. Turn `EADDRINUSE` into a one-line message naming the env var.
- Paths: resolve from `import.meta.url` (`fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url))`), not `process.cwd()`. `capture-preview.mjs`, `generate-social-card.mjs` and `verify-live.mjs` still write cwd-relative paths (`artifacts/`, `public/assets/social-card.png`, `dist`): run them from the repo root, and convert them when you touch them.
- Windows + Linux: `path.join`/`path.resolve` for file system paths, `replaceAll('\\', '/')` before comparing relative paths, `fileURLToPath` instead of `URL.pathname`.
- `build.mjs` removes only its own `dist/` behind an absolute-path guard; keep the guard. Builds and checks are offline.
- `check.mjs` is a guardrail (credential regexes, forbidden files, 3 MB limit, retired brand, CSP, no executable/input surface, banned claims, duplicate ids, link/anchor resolution). Add or tighten checks freely; never delete, loosen or bypass one to get green. Failure messages name the file and the rule.
- Network access is limited to: `capture-guide.mjs` (Google's public API-key docs, skipped with `--extension-only`), `verify-live.mjs` (production site) and Playwright browser downloads. Nothing reads `.env` or sends user data.
- Browser automation uses disposable profiles (`mkdtemp(tmpdir())`), owned localhost pages, no real keys, no personal profile. Wrap installed-extension capture in `node scripts/worktree/machine-lock.mjs capture -- …`.
- Verification scripts fail with a non-zero exit (`assert`/throw) and print a one-line JSON summary on success.
- Pure helpers get `node --test` tests next to them (`<name>.test.mjs`).
- Verify: `node --check <file>`, `npm run check`, plus the script's own run (e.g. `node scripts/capture-preview.mjs` after `npm run build`).
